_template: NOT AN APPROVAL. This documents the exact runtime legal-review document Andrew Miller must produce for the WAFT-validation runtime. The first waft-validation CI dispatch (runtime legal-review inputs left empty) generates legal-runtime/runtime-license-inventory.json and uploads it; Andrew reviews that exact inventory, then produces a real review JSON (drop the _template/_instructions keys, set reviewed:true, and set inventory_sha256 to the emitted inventory's SHA256). CI refuses to package while the review is absent, mismatched, reviewed!=true, or bound to a different inventory hash.
_instructions: Fields consumed by tools/p25_5/licenses.py validate-runtime-review: schema_id, inventory_sha256, reviewed, reviewer, reviewed_at, statement.
inventory_sha256: <64-hex SHA256 of legal-runtime/runtime-license-inventory.json emitted by the first waft-validation CI dispatch>
reviewed_at: <ISO-8601 UTC timestamp with explicit timezone, e.g. 2026-09-01T00:00:00Z>
statement: I, Andrew Miller, reviewed the generated WAFT-validation runtime license and notice inventory with SHA256 <hash>, including its conda packages (python, PyTorch CPU, torchvision, numpy, scipy, onnx, onnxruntime CPU, safetensors, timm, conda-pack, setuptools and their transitive natives). I approve this exact runtime inventory for the WAFT export/validation run. The pinned WAFT source is BSD-3-Clause; the WAFT checkpoint is operator-supplied and its file-level licence remains unknown -- this approval covers the packed conda+pip runtime only -- not the operator-supplied checkpoint, and not the WAFT source redistributed inside the package under waft-src/, which is separately covered by legal/source-legal-record.json.
